steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Mise-en-scene is a French term meaning 'everything placed in the frame' and includes setting, props, costume, makeup, lighting and the positioning and performance of actors.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Setting establishes time period, location, social context and atmosphere — it grounds the narrative and can function as a character itself.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Props carry symbolic meaning and can signal character traits, narrative development or thematic concerns; a motif is a recurring prop that gains significance through repetition.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Costume communicates identity, status, group belonging and character transformation across the film.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Don't just list mise-en-scene elements — explain what each one communicates to the audience. Use specific examples from the film: name the prop, describe the costume, identify the colour change. Show how mise-en-scene changes across scenes to track character or thematic development. Connect mise-en-scene to genre: how do setting, costume and props signal the film's genre conventions? Remember that mise-en-scene works with cinematography — a prop's meaning changes depending on how it is framed.
